While modern high-parameter Large Language Models (LLMs) such as GPT-4-Turbo have shown state-of-the-art WSD performance, their computational and energy demands limit scalability. This study investigates whether low-parameter LLMs (<4B parameters) can achieve comparable results through fine-tuning strategies that emphasize reasoning-driven sense identification. Using the FEWS dataset augmented with semi-automated, rationale-rich annotations, we fine-tune eight small-scale open-source LLMs (e.g. Gemma and Qwen). Our results reveal that Chain-of-Thought (CoT)-based reasoning combined with neighbour-word analysis achieves performance comparable to GPT-4-Turbo in zero-shot settings. Importantly, Gemma-3-4B and Qwen-3-4B models consistently outperform all medium-parameter baselines and state-of-the-art models on FEWS, with robust generalization to unseen senses. Furthermore, evaluation on the unseen "Fool Me If You Can'' dataset confirms strong cross-domain adaptability without task-specific fine-tuning. This work demonstrates that with carefully crafted reasoning-centric fine-tuning, low-parameter LLMs can deliver accurate WSD while substantially reducing computational and energy demands.

AI.tldr: Low-parameter LLMs (<4B) with reasoning-driven fine-tuning achieve GPT-4-Turbo-level WSD performance while being computationally efficient.
AI.motivation: Modern high-parameter LLMs like GPT-4-Turbo achieve state-of-the-art WSD but have prohibitive computational/energy costs, limiting scalability. There's a need to explore whether smaller models can match this performance through targeted fine-tuning strategies.
AI.method: Fine-tuned eight small-scale open-source LLMs (including Gemma and Qwen) using the FEWS dataset augmented with rationale-rich annotations. Employed Chain-of-Thought (CoT)-based reasoning combined with neighbour-word analysis to enhance sense identification.
AI.result: Gemma-3-4B and Qwen-3-4B consistently outperformed all medium-parameter baselines and state-of-the-art models on FEWS, achieving performance comparable to GPT-4-Turbo in zero-shot settings. Models showed robust generalization to unseen senses and strong cross-domain adaptability on the "Fool Me If You Can" dataset without task-specific fine-tuning.
AI.conclusion: Carefully crafted reasoning-centric fine-tuning enables low-parameter LLMs to deliver accurate WSD comparable to high-parameter models while substantially reducing computational and energy demands, offering a scalable solution for practical applications.

title: FlashAttention-4: Algorithm and Kernel Pipelining Co-Design for Asymmetric Hardware Scaling
summary: Attention, as a core layer of the ubiquitous Transformer architecture, is the bottleneck for large language models and long-context applications. While FlashAttention-3 optimized attention for Hopper GPUs through asynchronous execution and warp specialization, it primarily targets the H100 architecture. The AI industry has rapidly transitioned to deploying Blackwell-based systems such as the B200 and GB200, which exhibit fundamentally different performance characteristics due to asymmetric hardware scaling: tensor core throughput doubles while other functional units (shared memory bandwidth, exponential units) scale more slowly or remain unchanged. We develop several techniques to address these shifting bottlenecks on Blackwell GPUs: (1) redesigned pipelines that exploit fully asynchronous MMA operations and larger tile sizes, (2) software-emulated exponential and conditional softmax rescaling that reduces non-matmul operations, and (3) leveraging tensor memory and the 2-CTA MMA mode to reduce shared memory traffic and atomic adds in the backward pass. We demonstrate that our method, FlashAttention-4, achieves up to 1.3$\times$ speedup over cuDNN 9.13 and 2.7$\times$ over Triton on B200 GPUs with BF16, reaching up to 1613 TFLOPs/s (71% utilization). Beyond algorithmic innovations, we implement FlashAttention-4 entirely in CuTe-DSL embedded in Python, achieving 20-30$\times$ faster compile times compared to traditional C++ template-based approaches while maintaining full expressivity.

AI.tldr: FlashAttention-4 optimizes attention computation for Blackwell GPUs (B200/GB200) by addressing asymmetric hardware scaling through redesigned pipelines, software-emulated exponential operations, and tensor memory utilization, achieving 1.3-2.7× speedups over existing solutions while using CuTe-DSL for dramatically faster compilation.
AI.motivation: The transition from Hopper (H100) to Blackwell (B200/GB200) GPUs creates new bottlenecks due to asymmetric hardware scaling: tensor core throughput doubles while shared memory bandwidth and exponential units scale more slowly or remain unchanged, making existing FlashAttention-3 optimizations suboptimal for Blackwell architectures.
AI.method: Three key techniques: (1) Redesigned pipelines exploiting fully asynchronous MMA operations and larger tile sizes; (2) Software-emulated exponential and conditional softmax rescaling to reduce non-matmul operations; (3) Leveraging tensor memory and 2-CTA MMA mode to reduce shared memory traffic and atomic adds in backward pass. Implemented entirely in CuTe-DSL embedded in Python.
AI.result: Achieves up to 1.3× speedup over cuDNN 9.13 and 2.7× over Triton on B200 GPUs with BF16, reaching up to 1613 TFLOPs/s (71% utilization). Also achieves 20-30× faster compile times compared to traditional C++ template-based approaches while maintaining full expressivity.
AI.conclusion: FlashAttention-4 successfully addresses Blackwell GPU bottlenecks through algorithmic innovations and modern implementation techniques, demonstrating significant performance improvements for attention computation while providing a more efficient development workflow through CuTe-DSL.

title: DEBISS: a Corpus of Individual, Semi-structured and Spoken Debates
summary: The process of debating is essential in our daily lives, whether in studying, work activities, simple everyday discussions, political debates on TV, or online discussions on social networks. The range of uses for debates is broad. Due to the diverse applications, structures, and formats of debates, developing corpora that account for these variations can be challenging, and the scarcity of debate corpora in the state of the art is notable. For this reason, the current research proposes the DEBISS corpus: a collection of spoken and individual debates with semi-structured features. With a broad range of NLP task annotations, such as speech-to-text, speaker diarization, argument mining, and debater quality assessment.

AI.tldr: DEBISS corpus: A semi-structured spoken debate collection with comprehensive NLP annotations including speech-to-text, speaker diarization, argument mining, and debater quality assessment.
AI.motivation: Debates are ubiquitous in daily life across various domains, but existing debate corpora are scarce and don't adequately capture the diverse applications, structures, and formats of real-world debates.
AI.method: Creation of the DEBISS corpus - a collection of spoken and individual debates with semi-structured features, annotated for multiple NLP tasks including speech-to-text, speaker diarization, argument mining, and debater quality assessment.
AI.result: The paper introduces the DEBISS corpus as a comprehensive resource that addresses the scarcity of debate corpora by providing diverse debate formats with extensive NLP annotations.
AI.conclusion: The DEBISS corpus fills an important gap in debate resources by providing a versatile, annotated dataset that can support multiple NLP tasks and research in computational argumentation and debate analysis.

title: NCTB-QA: A Large-Scale Bangla Educational Question Answering Dataset and Benchmarking Performance
comment: 18 pages, 7 figures, 6 tables. Dataset contains 87,805 Bangla QA pairs from NCTB textbooks
summary: Reading comprehension systems for low-resource languages face significant challenges in handling unanswerable questions. These systems tend to produce unreliable responses when correct answers are absent from context. To solve this problem, we introduce NCTB-QA, a large-scale Bangla question answering dataset comprising 87,805 question-answer pairs extracted from 50 textbooks published by Bangladesh's National Curriculum and Textbook Board. Unlike existing Bangla datasets, NCTB-QA maintains a balanced distribution of answerable (57.25%) and unanswerable (42.75%) questions. NCTB-QA also includes adversarially designed instances containing plausible distractors. We benchmark three transformer-based models (BERT, RoBERTa, ELECTRA) and demonstrate substantial improvements through fine-tuning. BERT achieves 313% relative improvement in F1 score (0.150 to 0.620). Semantic answer quality measured by BERTScore also increases significantly across all models. Our results establish NCTB-QA as a challenging benchmark for Bangla educational question answering. This study demonstrates that domain-specific fine-tuning is critical for robust performance in low-resource settings.

AI.tldr: NCTB-QA is a new Bangla QA dataset with balanced answerable/unanswerable questions and adversarial distractors, showing transformer models achieve 313% F1 improvement with fine-tuning.
AI.motivation: Reading comprehension systems for low-resource languages struggle with unanswerable questions, producing unreliable responses when answers are absent from context. Existing Bangla datasets lack balanced unanswerable questions.
AI.method: Created NCTB-QA, a large-scale Bangla QA dataset with 87,805 question-answer pairs from 50 Bangladesh National Curriculum textbooks. Dataset maintains balanced distribution (57.25% answerable, 42.75% unanswerable) and includes adversarially designed instances with plausible distractors. Benchmarked three transformer models (BERT, RoBERTa, ELECTRA) with fine-tuning.
AI.result: Fine-tuning transformer models showed substantial improvements: BERT achieved 313% relative F1 improvement (0.150 to 0.620). Semantic answer quality measured by BERTScore increased significantly across all models. Domain-specific fine-tuning proved critical for robust performance in low-resource settings.
AI.conclusion: NCTB-QA establishes a challenging benchmark for Bangla educational question answering. The study demonstrates that domain-specific fine-tuning is essential for robust performance in low-resource language settings, particularly for handling unanswerable questions.

title: Leveraging LLM Parametric Knowledge for Fact Checking without Retrieval
summary: Trustworthiness is a core research challenge for agentic AI systems built on Large Language Models (LLMs). To enhance trust, natural language claims from diverse sources, including human-written text, web content, and model outputs, are commonly checked for factuality by retrieving external knowledge and using an LLM to verify the faithfulness of claims to the retrieved evidence. As a result, such methods are constrained by retrieval errors and external data availability, while leaving the models intrinsic fact-verification capabilities largely unused. We propose the task of fact-checking without retrieval, focusing on the verification of arbitrary natural language claims, independent of their source. To study this setting, we introduce a comprehensive evaluation framework focused on generalization, testing robustness to (i) long-tail knowledge, (ii) variation in claim sources, (iii) multilinguality, and (iv) long-form generation. Across 9 datasets, 18 methods and 3 models, our experiments indicate that logit-based approaches often underperform compared to those that leverage internal model representations. Building on this finding, we introduce INTRA, a method that exploits interactions between internal representations and achieves state-of-the-art performance with strong generalization. More broadly, our work establishes fact-checking without retrieval as a promising research direction that can complement retrieval-based frameworks, improve scalability, and enable the use of such systems as reward signals during training or as components integrated into the generation process.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces fact-checking without retrieval, proposing INTRA method that leverages internal model representations to verify claims without external knowledge retrieval, achieving state-of-the-art performance across diverse datasets and demonstrating strong generalization capabilities.
AI.motivation: Current fact-checking methods rely on external knowledge retrieval, which is constrained by retrieval errors and data availability while underutilizing LLMs' intrinsic fact-verification capabilities. The paper aims to develop retrieval-free fact-checking that can verify arbitrary natural language claims independent of their source.
AI.method: The paper introduces INTRA (Internal Representation Analysis), a method that exploits interactions between internal model representations for fact-checking without retrieval. It establishes a comprehensive evaluation framework testing robustness to long-tail knowledge, claim source variation, multilinguality, and long-form generation. The approach compares 18 methods across 9 datasets and 3 models.
AI.result: Experiments show logit-based approaches underperform compared to methods leveraging internal representations. INTRA achieves state-of-the-art performance with strong generalization across diverse evaluation settings, demonstrating the viability of retrieval-free fact-checking as a complementary approach to retrieval-based frameworks.
AI.conclusion: Fact-checking without retrieval is a promising research direction that can complement retrieval-based frameworks, improve scalability, and enable integration as reward signals during training or as components in the generation process. INTRA's success highlights the value of leveraging internal model representations for robust fact verification.

title: Reasoning Theater: Disentangling Model Beliefs from Chain-of-Thought
summary: We provide evidence of performative chain-of-thought (CoT) in reasoning models, where a model becomes strongly confident in its final answer, but continues generating tokens without revealing its internal belief. Our analysis compares activation probing, early forced answering, and a CoT monitor across two large models (DeepSeek-R1 671B & GPT-OSS 120B) and find task difficulty-specific differences: The model's final answer is decodable from activations far earlier in CoT than a monitor is able to say, especially for easy recall-based MMLU questions. We contrast this with genuine reasoning in difficult multihop GPQA-Diamond questions. Despite this, inflection points (e.g., backtracking, 'aha' moments) occur almost exclusively in responses where probes show large belief shifts, suggesting these behaviors track genuine uncertainty rather than learned "reasoning theater." Finally, probe-guided early exit reduces tokens by up to 80% on MMLU and 30% on GPQA-Diamond with similar accuracy, positioning attention probing as an efficient tool for detecting performative reasoning and enabling adaptive computation.

AI.tldr: The paper reveals "performative chain-of-thought" where models show high confidence early but continue generating tokens, and demonstrates that activation probing can detect this performative reasoning and enable early exit to reduce computation.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether chain-of-thought reasoning in large language models represents genuine reasoning or is merely "performative" - where models continue generating tokens after already being confident in their answer, potentially wasting computational resources.
AI.method: Used activation probing, early forced answering, and CoT monitoring across two large models (DeepSeek-R1 671B & GPT-OSS 120B) on MMLU (easy recall) and GPQA-Diamond (difficult multihop) questions. Analyzed when final answers become decodable from activations and tracked inflection points in reasoning.
AI.result: Found task-specific differences: For easy MMLU questions, final answers decodable far earlier in CoT than monitors can detect. For difficult GPQA-Diamond, genuine reasoning observed. Inflection points correlate with large belief shifts in probes. Probe-guided early exit reduced tokens by 80% on MMLU and 30% on GPQA-Diamond with similar accuracy.
AI.conclusion: Attention probing serves as an efficient tool for detecting performative reasoning and enabling adaptive computation, allowing models to exit early when they've already reached confident answers, significantly reducing computational overhead while maintaining accuracy.
